The Rundown offers a sharp contrast of perspectives you won’t hear anywhere else, and a daily commentary you can't miss, we deliver the full picture of the day's biggest events.

item.title: Are Changes Coming to ICE?
item.description:
Despite Republican midterm setbacks and demographic shifts among suburban and Hispanic voters, President Trump has doubled down on hardline immigration enforcement. Former Acting ICE Director Todd Lyons speaks with FOX News congressional correspondent Bill Melugin to analyze the political fallout and ICE’s operational pivot toward discreet interior enforcement. Lyons also discusses whether immigration policies cost Republicans at the ballot box, and outlines his opposition to mass amnesty for immigration offenses.
This Veterans Day, political battles in Washington over Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s military decisions are colliding with urgent questions about how America truly supports its troops. Marine veteran and Medal of Honor recipient Dakota Meyer defends Hegseth against congressional attacks, outlines his new mission leading a military task force to overhaul squalid living conditions in troop barracks, and explains why prioritizing the needs of service members is essential to restoring trust and military readiness.
PLUS, commentary by Jason Chaffetz, FOX News contributor and the host of the Jason In The House podcast on FOX News Radio.

item.title: Israel's New Knesset, Netanyahu Rival Chosen to Form Government
item.description:
Israel's new Knesset has been sworn in. Gadi Eisenkot is seeking support to replace Benjamin Netanyahu and is negotiating with potential partners to quickly form a coalition. He intends to advance two initiatives before the government is established: a state commission of inquiry into October 7th and a repeal of the judicial overhaul. This Knesset also includes a record number of Arab members, and Iran remains a significant concern for the next government.
FOX's Eben Brown speaks with Ruthie Blum, a contributing editor at the 'Jerusalem News Syndicate', cohost of the 'Israel Undiplomatic' podcast, and is a former adviser at the office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who explains how the Israeli political system works.

item.title: "Honey Pot" Espionage? NVIDIA Scandal Raises Questions About National Security"
item.description:
Reports indicate U.S. business leaders face serious vulnerability as Chinese intelligence services target major tech firms in an aggressive espionage campaign. Fox News Contributor and former CIA Station Chief Dan Hoffman explains how honey traps and compromising operations are used to extract sensitive trade secrets, the urgency of an official FBI damage assessment, and what the fallout means for broader U.S.-China relations ahead of potential bilateral talks. (edited)Following a tough election cycle for Republicans, leadership battles and unfinished business are taking center stage on Capitol Hill. Florida Republican Senator Rick Scott joins the Rundown to unpack what went wrong for the GOP and why voters are anxious about things like affordability, and why he believes the party must settle on a clear agenda before picking its leadership team.
Plus, commentary by Ted Jenkin, President of Exit Stage Left Advisors and Host of The Red, White & Green Show

item.title: Antisemitic Protests Target Jewish Owned Restaurants in Philadelphia
item.description:
A "boycott ride" targeting Jewish-owned and Israel-connected restaurants in Philadelphia took place over the weekend, and was drowned out by drowned out by hundreds of pro-Israel counter protesters. It was organized by an anti-Zionist cycling group called Philly Bike On Your Left and the event called for a boycott of six local businesses. Roughly 300 pro-Palestinian/boycott demonstrators faced off against an estimated 200 to 300 pro-Israel counter protesters and community members. Long lines of patrons formed outside the targeted businesses as a show of solidarity.
FOX's Eben Brown speaks with Marti Lieberman, owner and founder of The Mac Mart in Philadelphia, who says it was scary, but she and her team got incredible support by their loyal patrons and others.

item.title: Stephen Miller, The Data Center Dilemma, And Republican Regrets

item.itunes:author: FOX News Podcasts
item.content:encoded:
In the wake of tough midterm setbacks, the GOP faces an urgent reckoning over where its message and strategy fell short. Representative Tim Burchett (R-TN) joins The Rundown to deliver a candid autopsy of the GOP’s campaign missteps, explaining why missed opportunities on gas affordability and congressional stock trading cost them with voters. He also breaks down his push to give communities control over the boom of AI data centers, reacts to Stephen Miller stepping in as White House Chief of Staff, and discusses whether he is ready to fill Tennessee’s newly open U.S. Senate seat. 


Is a traditional four-year degree losing its grip on the American workforce? As tuition costs climb, a deficit of skilled workers has more Americans pivoting toward trade careers. Former Pennsylvania Congressman Jason Altmire—now President and CEO of Career Education Colleges and Universities—joins the Rundown to discuss what’s driving the nationwide labor shortage, which trade jobs are most in demand, and how alternative programs train skilled workers faster and at a fraction of the cost of a university degree.

 

PLUS, commentary by Karol Markowicz, columnist for the New York Post.

item.title: Beyond the Memes: Unpacking the Rise and Fall of Elizabeth Holmes
item.description:
There’s a ton of buzz right now surrounding "You Can See Everything"—the new documentary about Elizabeth Holmes.
More than a decade ago, Holmes and her company, Theranos, promised a medical revolution with blood-testing technology that ultimately collapsed into a multi-billion-dollar fraud. In 2022, a jury convicted her on four counts of criminal fraud, and she is currently serving an 11-year sentence in federal prison.
"You Can See Everything" takes a close-up look at her life before prison and where things stand today, inspiring a new wave of online chatter and memes.
Recently on the FOX Business Rundown, FOX Business’s Lydia Hu spoke with Wall Street Journal reporter Christopher Weaver, who was part of the paper's original investigation into Theranos. He unpacked the rise and fall of Elizabeth Holmes, explaining why her story still captivates the public all these years later.
Whether you’ve watched the documentary or not, there is plenty to learn from this conversation.
It originally aired on the FOX Business Rundown podcast, but we thought it was worth sharing right here on the FOX News Rundown Extra.
